spec_match.rationale: Uses the exact WICG modern-algos surface — generateKey({name:'ML-KEM-768'|'ML-KEM-1024'}), encapsulateBits() destructured to {ciphertext, sharedKey}, decapsulateBits(), and raw-public export — matching the spec's KEM shape and the chromestatus algorithm list.

interactive.rationale: Parameter-set select, run and reset buttons drive a three-party stage that fills real hex artifacts, byte lengths, and a constant-time secrets-match badge.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises keypair generation, encapsulate/decapsulate, and both parties deriving the same secret without transmitting it; the page walks exactly that flow.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles the unsupported browser honestly (flag note with exact flag + origin-trial token, err status, no fake output), reports real exception name/message on failure, and even covers the theoretical secrets-mismatch branch.

references.rationale: Rich sibling cross-links, but unlike other features' concept pages the see-also omits a direct https://chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 link — it lives only on the feature index, weakening the per-page self-heal contract.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the encapsulateBits/decapsulateBits typeofs and the secure-context gate matching this page's contract; in this unflagged Chromium 141 session it reads 1 pass / 7 fail, all failures being the expected absent WebCryptoPQC surface.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): desktop screenshot shows the visible flag note and honest warn status with untouched em-dash artifacts, zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; the run button and the flagged success path could not be driven interactively here.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert reports unsupported runs, secrets-match with the parameter set, and run failures with the error name.

design_system.rationale: All colours are CSS variables, but the default-visible warn status (--accent-amber on --bg-stone) computes ~3.5:1 and the flagged-path match badge (--bg-ivory on --accent-emerald) ~4.0:1 — both under WCAG AA 4.5:1 at their 0.72–0.8rem bold sizes.

accessibility.rationale: role=status aria-live on the status line, aria-live on the key artifact cells, a labelled select, and native buttons; state is conveyed as text plus colour, never colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow (hex blocks word-break and the control row wraps); desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental fonts.googleapis.com request fails.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus feature link to this page's see-also
openQuestions.detail: CLAUDE.md invariant 3 wants every page to carry the chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 link as the slug self-heal anchor; this concept (like its four webcrypto siblings) links siblings only. Add the ChromeStatus entry to the see-also list — a one-line additive fix.

openQuestions.title: Bring the warn status and success badge up to WCAG AA contrast
openQuestions.detail: status-line.warn renders --accent-amber #b87b00 on --bg-stone #f4f3ee at 0.8rem bold, ~3.5:1, and is the default visible state in every unflagged browser; match-badge.ok renders --bg-ivory on --accent-emerald #0a8f5c, ~4.0:1, on the flagged success path. Both miss AA 4.5:1 for text this small. Darkening the amber/emerald usage or switching badge text to --text-black on emerald (5.1:1) fixes it; the same pattern repeats across all five webcrypto concept pages.

openQuestions.title: Capture the flagged success path in a WebCryptoPQC-enabled Chrome 150+
openQuestions.detail: This session's Chromium 141 cannot expose ML-KEM, so the generate/encapsulate/decapsulate flow, key sizes (1184/1568-byte public keys, 32-byte secrets), and the match badge were not observed live. Run once with --enable-blink-features=WebCryptoPQC on Chrome 150+ and record the artifacts as evidence.

summary: A faithful, well-staged ML-KEM encapsulation demo using the real WICG modern-algos methods with an honest flag-note fallback and constant-time secret comparison. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): honest warn state renders, zero console errors, no unintended failed requests, no overflow at 360×740 DPR3 or 1280×800. Open items: add the per-page chromestatus link, fix the sub-AA amber/emerald contrast pairs, and record flagged-browser success evidence.
